item.title: Backlash to ICE agreement persists in Springdale, a month after police-prompted detention
item.description: Springdale Borough is one of two Allegheny County municipalities formally cooperating with ICE, as some neighboring towns and the county at large have adopted noncooperation policies.

item.title: Pa. lawmakers seek to build on infrastructure to meet energy demands
item.description: Two proposals floated by state lawmakers wouldn’t require any new power plants or transmission lines, but could add to the supply.

item.title: From a Carnegie town hall: A hunger for close-to-home news and accountability
item.description: It’s difficult to get around without a car, and the scarcity of neighborhood news often makes meaningful public participation arduous.

item.title: From a virtual town hall: AI raises concerns in society, journalism
item.description: A Pittsburgh’s Public Source town hall done via Zoom drew attendees from Greensburg to Baltimore, and questions about the evolution of local news were similarly wide-ranging.

item.title: How Shell’s cracker has polluted more than permitted with no new fines for three years
item.description: A Beaver County ethylene plant operated by Shell Polymers Monaca continues to exceed limits on nitrogen oxide, as the official permitting process drags.

item.title: From an Oakmont town hall: Fracking to front porches, and a yen for journalism that connects
item.description: Local media can be a glue that helps communities to come together, according to people who came out for the seventh and final “You Have the Floor” event in Oakmont.

item.title: Don’t let return-to-office fever push women out of the workforce
item.description: The workplace has changed over six years, and some of the shifts were good — for women especially. Pittsburgh employers shouldn’t throw out flexibility in a rush to return to 2019 norms.

item.title: Pitt students built a website to scrutinize landlords — theirs, and maybe yours
item.description: Rate Yinz Landlord is intended for Pitt students but available for all renters in Pittsburgh, which has failed to implement mandatory rental inspections.

item.title: ICE training at Pittsburgh International, expected at checkpoint Tuesday
item.description: Security was running smoothly with minimal lines throughout the morning a day after Pittsburgh was included in a list of 14 airports at which ICE would be assisting.

item.title: How historic overtime payments in 2025 drove up Pittsburgh’s budget
item.description: Last year 105 City of Pittsburgh employees took home total compensation topping $200,000, thanks largely to a second year of historic overtime outlays.
